content.key_idea: GPU execution is a hierarchy: streams queue kernels' CTAs, a CTA scheduler assigns them to SMs, and within each SM a warp scheduler dispatches warps to execution units while memory flows L1 to L2 to DRAM.
content.reading_order: left to right across streams and kernels, down through the CTA scheduler into the GPU's SMs and memory hierarchy, then into the zoomed SM panel on the right

evidence: The GPU's hardware is arranged in a hierarchy that supports execution at a scale of hundreds
The main processor unit of a GPU is a Streaming Multiprocessor (SM), with modern GPUs
A group of 32 threads make up a warp, which typically execute concurrently in lockstep.

summary: Figure 5 of the POD-Attention paper illustrates the generic GPU execution model that motivates the work, not POD-Attention's own contribution. Two streams each queue kernels (Kernel A, B, C); a CTA scheduler pulls queued CTAs from these kernels and assigns them to the GPU's Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), each holding executing CTAs and an L1 cache/shared-memory partition that feeds a shared L2 cache and DRAM. A zoomed panel on the right expands one SM to show its warp pool, warp scheduler, execution units, and load/store unit, illustrating how the warp scheduler dispatches eligible warps every cycle. The diagram uses green boxes for CTA/warp/execution-unit elements, orange boxes for the memory hierarchy, and blue boxes to highlight the two scheduling components, with dashed borders grouping the streams and the warp pool.
summary_zh: 图5展示GPU的通用执行模型作为背景铺垫:两个流分别排队若干内核,CTA调度器将排队CTA分配到各SM;右侧放大单个SM,展示warp池、warp调度器、执行单元与访存单元。绿色表示CTA/warp/执行单元,橙色表示缓存与DRAM,蓝色突出两个调度器组件。
notes: This is a background diagram of generic GPU hardware/execution, not a depiction of POD-Attention's own novel design.
